# zha-device-handlers: many device quirks report the wrong state — diagnose and repair without a test suite

This software sits between my home automation hub and a pile of oddly-behaved wireless gadgets, and its whole job is to smooth over each gadget's peculiarities so the hub sees sensible numbers and sensible notifications. After moving to the current build a lot of my gadgets started showing nonsense in the UI, so I went through them one at a time with a listener attached to see exactly what was emitted. Nothing about my hardware, my hub or the radio traffic is any different. The repository has received 20 separate undocumented edits.

Plenty goes wrong just watching values arrive. On a sensor watching for a fire hazard, feeding a hazard figure in on the vendor's private channel still surfaces it there, but the standard alarm-state report that used to accompany it never arrives now, for the alarm-raised and the alarm-cleared figures alike. A sensor for fine dust in the air has an implausibly-high cut-off that is off by one step: a sample one unit above the old cut-off is now published instead of dropped, while a sample exactly at the cut-off is still accepted as before. A gadget that senses both passers-by and room brightness gets brightness wrong in two independent ways: a raw zero and a mid-range raw figure that used to collapse to the same floor now both come out one higher than they should, and, separately, the growth of the curve itself is broken, so the two biggest
